thread:
sam: quick note from today's sync — exploring a 'precision negotiator' that sits in the planner and publishes a tiny policy blob per model version. goal: enable fp8/int8/4bit safely, limit blast radius, and keep cache compat. looking for edge-cases.

trina: love the idea. one sticky bit: KV cache binary layout changes between bitpaths. do we version cache keys or keep a universal on-disk format?

sam: leaning to versioned cache keys: <model-v>#<bitpath-v>#<kv-hash>. That way runtime can decide to skip cache if incompatible. downside: higher cache miss rate when we change bitpath.

leo: +1 for key-versioning. ops implication: cache storage growth during rollout. we need a background reclaim job and a retention policy tied to canary state.

rashmi: also consider a small transcoder for hot sessions: if we detect a mismatch but session is active and important, attempt async transcoding of cached KV from old->new bitpath. this reduces tail latency for premium users.

trina: transcoder idea is neat but risky for correctness. need a verified conversion layer and tests for numerical drift. maybe only allow transcoder for int8<->fp8 and not for 4bit->others initially.

sam: agreed. limit to safe conversions. we'll mark module-level conversions allowed in policy. e.g., encoder: no-transcode, decoder: allow-transcode.

leo: runtime perf note: activating transcoder will spike GPU/CPU; schedule it on low-priority workers and throttle. add metrics: transcoder-ops, transcoder-latency, transcoder-failures.

rashmi: API surface: callers can pass quality_hint: best_quality | balanced | economize. planner maps to bitpath candidate list. default mapping lives in model policy.

sam: here's a sample policy shape (simple JSON) — please don't copy proto exactly but gives the idea:

{"model":"copper-vision-1","default":"int8","allowed":["fp8","int8","4bit"],"min_for_tenant":{"acme":"int8"},"module_policy":{"vision_encoder":"fp16","decoder":"fp8"},"ramp":{"enabled":true,"deg_threshold":0.08,"lookback":16}}

trina: keep the policy backward compatible. include a version integer and unknown-field ignoring. also store an admin-change timestamp for audit.

leo: decision logic for planner: score each candidate bitpath by expected_cost_saving - penalty_for_latency - expected_deg_risk * risk_weight. we need a small regression model to tune weights.

sam: love the cost model idea. ops: can we get a lightweight perf oracle from infra? numbers per bitpath and seq_len distribution to feed planner.

ops-bot: infra-metrics: added per-kernel perf table to /infra/metrics/precision-oracle. Link: https://infra/metrics/precision-oracle

rashmi: safety/fallback order proposal: 1) try chosen bitpath; 2) if deg_score spike > X, retry on int8 variant without changing client-visible model_id; 3) if still bad, route to queued high-fidelity host pool; 4) if extreme, return error with suggestion to client to request best_quality. document will list thresholds.

trina: add a probe that runs shadow-evals: mirror 10% of requests to shadow-pool with conservative bitpath and compute delta_quality metric. alert if delta_quality > threshold.

sam: exactly what I was thinking. make sure shadowing is cheap (sampled) and tied to eval anchors per product.

leo: rollout strategy: 1) internal-only bench, 2) dev tenants, 3) 1% canary, 4) 10% with shadowing, 5) gradual increase. tie cache pruning to rollout phases to reclaim storage.

rashmi: ops playbook bullets: auto-rollback if rolling delta_quality exceeds 2x baseline or tail latency + p95 > 15% for 2 mins. also manual stop button on console.

trina: testing checklist: unit planner scoring, simulate cache miss/mismatch, transcoder correctness suites (quantization error bounds), canary shadow-reporting, and long-term storage growth test.

sam: question: permit tokenwise bitpath changes? risky for cache; maybe allow only stateless calls and only when module_policy allows. tokenwise hysteresis possible later.

leo: if we do tokenwise control, add a small hysteresis buffer and require no cache usage. and emit chosen_bitpath per-token in telemetry to debug.

ops-bot: created ticket: infra#3422 precision-oracle integration + canary config. Canary link: https://infra/redwood/canaries/precision-negotiator-3422

rashmi: final ask: can someone draft the RFC follow-up summarizing policy fields, telemetry keys (chosen_bitpath, policy_version, cache_key_v, transcoder_used, deg_score, quality_delta, p95_latency) and fallback order? I'll coordinate with legal for audit fields.

sam: I'll draft and drop in docs repo. tagging @eng-ml for review. thanks everyone :sparkles:
